hook_text: Every roll you sell before number fourteen belongs to the braai man. Here's why.
clip_script: You want to sell boerewors rolls at the taxi rank on Saturday. Before roll number one, Saturday has already cost you: R400 for the braai and stand, R258 for the gazebo and cooler boxes. R658 gone — and you have sold nothing. That is your pile of stones, and it does not care how your day goes. Every roll carries its own costs with it — wors, bread, sauce, serviette, R48 a roll. Sell at R95 and each roll leaves R47 in your pocket. That R47 is the contribution — not profit, not yet. It is one stone lifted off the pile. So the only question that matters at six in the morning: how many rolls until the pile is gone? R658 divided by R47 — fourteen. Rolls one to fourteen, you are working for the braai man. Roll fifteen is the first roll you sell for yourself. A shoe factory is the same sum with more zeros: pile of R658 000, R47 a pair, survival line at 14 000 pairs against a plan of 24 000. And when the wors price rises or a big buyer demands a discount, the line MOVES — so you calculate before you commit. Break-even is not a report card. It is a headlight.
visual_style: A dawn taxi-rank stand with an actual pile of stones shrinking roll by roll, a chalk counter ticking to fourteen, then zooming out to a factory running the same sum in bigger numerals; smoky braai palette with headlight beams.
pacing: Stone-by-stone countdown, a triumphant beat at roll fifteen, then quick what-if line shifts.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find your own roll number fourteen.
